name: Progressive Encephalomyelitis with Rigidity and Myoclonus
aliases: Progressive Encephalomyelitis with Rigidity and Myoclonus Syndrome

criteria.description: Progressive rigidity of axial and limb muscles with stimulus-sensitive myoclonus
Brainstem signs including dysarthria, dysphagia, and oculomotor abnormalities
Presence of anti-glycine receptor antibodies or other relevant neuronal autoantibodies in serum or CSF
CSF pleocytosis or elevated protein indicating central nervous system inflammation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive rigidity with myoclonus and brainstem signs plus detection of relevant neuronal autoantibodies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is supported by exclusion of alternative causes and response to immunotherapy.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive axial and limb muscle rigidity
searchTerms: stiff muscles in body and limbs

pathognomonic.symptomName: Brainstem dysfunction including dysarthria and dysphagia
searchTerms: brainstem problems causing speech and swallowing issues
difficulty speaking and swallowing from brainstem
dysarthria and dysphagia due to brainstem dysfunction
dysfunction causing abnormal heart rate and sweating
muscle stiffness in arms and legs
weakness or pain in hands and feet
nerve damage symptoms in arms or legs
eye movement problems like shaking or paralysis
abnormal eye motions such as nystagmus or ophthalmoplegia

occasional.symptomName: Mood disturbances including anxiety and depression
searchTerms: mood changes including sadness and worry
gastrointestinal issues due to autonomic failure

rare.symptomName: Respiratory failure due to brainstem involvement
searchTerms: difficulty breathing due to brainstem injury
respiratory arrest caused by brain problems

rare.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias secondary to autonomic dysfunction
searchTerms: heart rhythm problems from autonomic issues
irregular heartbeat due to nerve dysfunction

rare.symptomName: Cutaneous manifestations such as rash related to paraneoplastic syndrome
searchTerms: skin rash linked to cancer-related syndrome
cutaneous rash from immune response to tumor

laboratory: Detection of anti-glycine receptor antibodies in serum or CSF
Elevated inflammatory markers in some cases
imaging: MRI brain may show nonspecific T2 hyperintensities in brainstem or spinal cord
Normal or mild atrophy in advanced stages
genetic: No known genetic mutations directly associated; primarily autoimmune etiology
other: Electromyography showing continuous motor unit activity
Positive response to immunotherapy (e.g., corticosteroids, IVIG, plasmapheresis)

distinguishingFeatures: Typically associated with anti-GAD antibodies rather than anti-glycine receptor antibodies
Lack of specific autoantibodies seen in PERM

redFlags: Development of brainstem signs including respiratory compromise
Failure to respond to symptomatic treatment without immunotherapy
